items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1961-04-07
items.q: Piku got it from a piccolo part, from a band, it was all written

ctx.x: So there wasn't any Dixieland orchestrated music that you could buy if you had the money?

For marching, for a saints go marching in? No. I see. There wasn't nothing like that. Same as a high society. There wasn't a, no orchestration for high society. High society, piku, you know, like the military band was part, marching band. Mm-hmm. Piku, taking the piccolo part, you see, that could have been written by Susie, or some of the other great writers, you see. I see. He taking the piccolo part and rearranged a clarinet part. Now I don't know whether it was high society's name or not, but that's the name…
and made a new piece out of the melody line. Yeah. And made clarendina everybody,

items.title: William "Ba Ba" Ridgley Interview, 1959-06-02
items.q: I like Piku, yeah. He's good. Nice fella. Funny.

ctx.x: I knew him. He was with the... The clarinet player downtown. What's his name? Old, old, old man. Piku? Piku. Them was brothers, you see. Them was two fellas. And you hired them to play and somebody would say, well, we're going to have a third of supper at Kawano over there. And they said to somebody. Piku, you blow up anybody's job to go drink wine. He's a fine fella. I like Piku, yeah. He's good. Nice fella. Funny. Comical. Could not tremble on for his... I don't see...
How was Beth DeLeo? Was he a good reader? Oh, yeah, yeah, yeah.
